# UX waves: scheduling the work that makes every mockup real

Companion to [`ux-coverage.md`](ux-coverage.md) (what must be built, and what exists) and `node check.mjs --ux` (live status). This file orders the **206 UX work packages** that remain (every open owner of a mockup screen, hosted surface, kit board or framework, brand rule or owner rule, plus the open dependencies they need) into waves the lead can dispatch.

## 1. How the waves are built

- **Set.** 206 packages: 168 owners of UX items and 38 prerequisites they depend on. Parked, not scheduled: 27 optional or deferred packages (CM-\*, UK-55, UK-60, UK-61, ...), listed in section 8.
- **Order.** Hard dependencies from `workpackages.json`, plus two UX-order rules that are _not_ graph edges (a screen built before the shell it lives in is built twice): every console UI builder waits for **ST-48** (shell v2) and **UK-58** (tokens), every portal builder waits for **UK-58**. The lead honours them; `--ready` does not know them.
- **Parallelism.** At most **8** builders at once. Lane caps: worker 3, console 3, ui 3, portal 2, sdk 2, docs 2, cli-ci 2, godot 1, native 1. README section 5 hotspots: one corpus/parity/plan-mode package at a time, one migration at a time, and nothing else in the console lane while ST-48 rewrites the shell.
- **Clock.** A package takes its upper estimate in weeks; a plan-mode package whose plan is not approved adds 0.5 week for the planner. A wave is a 2-week window of starts, so later waves are a forecast, wave 1 is a commitment.
- **Gate.** A package that builds screens is done only when `pkey-ux-reviewer` passes the built screens and `node check.mjs --ux-review <ID> pass "<evidence>"` records it; `--set <ID> done` refuses otherwise.

### Sensitivity: the corpus lane is the bottleneck

README section 5 allows one corpus-touching package at a time (every plan-mode package and every package gated `corpus`). Of the 206 packages here, 60.7 weeks of upper-estimate work is corpus-touching, and many of them (the I-, U-, LX-, HA- and SP- families) are exactly the backends the console and portal screens need. Serialised, that lane alone sets the calendar:

| Corpus-touching packages in flight | Forecast (weeks) |
| ---------------------------------- | ---------------- |
| 1                                  | 68.2             |
| 2                                  | 39.6             |
| 3                                  | 39.6             |

**Recommendation for the lead:** keep one corpus _owner_ but batch: plan the wire changes of two or three of these packages together and regenerate the corpus once per wave. That is what takes the forecast from 68.2 to about 39.6 weeks. This is a lead decision, not a graph change.
